reason: The Sun can drive evaporation from the ocean, beginning the water cycle.
expectation: Ocean water will be lifted into the air as vapor.

effect: Evaporation gives me a way to move ocean water into the atmosphere.
reason: Air is a plausible partner for evaporated water as it moves toward clouds and rain.
expectation: This may form clouds or moisture in the atmosphere.

effect: Clouds provide the next stage of the water cycle; their visible droplets form when vapor condenses.
reaction: The distinction between invisible vapor and visible droplets was useful.
reason: Gravity is a plausible way to bring water from clouds back to the ground as rain.

effect: Rainfall brings the water cycle back to land, suggesting a route toward rivers.
reaction: The link between gravity gathering worlds and bringing rain down was satisfying.
reason: Rainfall on Earth is a plausible starting point for runoff and rivers.
expectation: Rainfall on land will produce runoff or a river.

effect: Rainfall combines with gravity to create rivers, providing a route toward the delta.
reaction: The automatic correction made the intended role of gravity clear.
reason: Rivers meeting the ocean can deposit sediment and build a delta.
expectation: The rivers may form a delta where they reach the ocean.

effect: Rivers do not combine directly with the ocean; Earth and Sun are available partners.
reaction: I expected the river mouth to be the direct route to a delta.
reason: Earth is the more plausible source of sediment for rivers to carry toward a delta.
expectation: The rivers will pick up sediment or otherwise progress toward forming a delta.

alternatives.reason: This might help keep water travelling, but Earth seems more relevant to the delta.

effect: Rivers and Earth produced sediment, suggesting it can now be deposited at the ocean.
reaction: The intermediate step makes the delta's construction clearer.
reason: Sediment carried to the ocean can accumulate at a river mouth and build a delta.
expectation: The sediment will form a delta at the coast.

effect: Sediment meeting the ocean formed a delta and completed that goal; the water-travel goal remains.
reaction: The sediment-to-land progression was satisfying and clear.
reason: Rivers and Sun were previously identified as compatible, and solar energy helps keep water moving through the cycle.
expectation: This will advance or complete the continuing water cycle.

effect: Rivers and Sun completed the water cycle and the remaining goal, tying solar energy and gravity together.
reaction: The closing image of a cycle continuing without my intervention was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making sediment and then a delta was most worthwhile: the intermediate step made the creation of new land understandable rather than magical.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying rivers directly with the ocean was a little frustrating because the river mouth seemed a plausible place to form a delta, though the compatibility feedback gave me a useful next lead.

surprise.text: I was surprised that rainfall needed gravity rather than Earth to make rivers; the automatic correction highlighted gravity's role in carrying water downhill.

arbitrary.text: Rivers plus Sun to make the whole water cycle felt somewhat compressed as a recipe, although the explanation connected sunlight and gravity to the broader process.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue: the clear sediment-to-delta progression and the prospect of a world developing without constant intervention make the next developments appealing.
